attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The wording and qualifiers match the source. But the sentence describes AI data centers that might succeed someday ('even if they somehow succeed'), with value words and an undefined margin. It is not a report on a specific period, so labelling it an observation is wrong.

contract.note: The contract supplies a gross-margin basis and a Q4 2025 reporting period that the speaker never gave. It also tests a hypothetical about successful projects against one operator's reported results. Whether he looks right or wrong would depend on those choices, so the plain reading stretches what he actually said.

evidence.note: Genuine CoreWeave FY2025 10-K showing a six-year equipment life. The derived 71.68% ratio covers the full year, not Q4, leaves out technology and infrastructure costs, and comes from one operator, so it neither proves nor disproves a 70% ceiling.

reviews.rationale: This is a judgment about data centers that might succeed someday. It mixes value words with a '70% at best' ceiling on a margin he never defines, and its obsolescence clause is hedged ('might'). Scoring it requires a margin basis and period the speaker did not supply. The only evidence item is context: a different period and a different cost boundary.
